name: MonarchChatDock
title: ChatDock
summary: Chat that stays one tap away on any screen: a floating action button with the unread count that opens the chat in a bottom sheet. The app supplies the chat.
whenToUse: In an app that offers its team chat (Rook Chat or its own screens) from every screen.
whenNotToUse: For a chat that is the main screen of the app, use the collaboration components in a full screen. For a single conversation thread, use MonarchThreadPanel.
api: @Composable fun MonarchChatDock(open: Boolean, onOpenChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, unread: Int = 0, loading: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, loadingLabel: String? = null, icon: @Composable () -> Unit = { MonarchIcon(MonarchGlyphs.ChatBubble, contentDescription = null) }, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

options.name: open
options.description: Whether the chat sheet is shown.

options.name: onOpenChange
options.description: Called with true when the launcher is tapped and false when the sheet is dismissed.

options.name: unread
options.description: Unread messages; 0 shows no badge, more than 99 shows "99+".

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a spinner and "Loading chat…" in the sheet instead of the content.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the launcher and the sheet. null uses "Rook Chat".

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: The text while loading. null uses "Loading chat…".

states.name: closed
states.description: The launcher with its count badge.

states.name: open
states.description: A bottom sheet with the chat.

states.name: loading
states.description: The sheet shows a spinner and "Loading chat…".

appearance: The launcher is the inverse surface with inverse content, as the web's dark launcher; the badge is the danger solid with its on-solid text. The sheet uses MonarchBottomSheet's roles. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ChatDock embeds the Rook Chat web app in an iframe that stays alive behind the launcher, with a postMessage protocol for unread counts, calls and sessions. On Android the app supplies the chat in the content slot and reports unread and loading itself; the sheet content is composed while the sheet is open and is not kept alive when it closes. Incoming call prompts are not part of this component.
accessibility: The launcher is read as the label and the unread count, such as "Rook Chat, 3 unread"; the badge itself is not read again.
The sheet is a pane named by the label.
While loading, the spinner is read as "Loading chat…".
edgeCases: A negative unread count shows no badge.
Keeping the chat state across opening and closing is the app's job.
